title: They complained about food. God answered with fire in the flesh.
paragraphs: They complained about food. God answered with fire in the flesh.

Not because He was cruel.
Because their rebellion was no longer small.
Numbers 21:5–6 is terrifying for a reason.

Israel did not just grumble about the wilderness.
They spoke against God.
They despised the bread He provided.
They treated mercy like trash.
That is the real poison.

Not the snakes first.
The pride.

They said, “Why have you brought us up out of Egypt to die?”
As if bondage was better than obedience.
As if slavery was sweeter than trusting God.
As if heaven’s provision was beneath them.
And then the serpents came.

Suddenly the people felt in their bodies what sin had already done in their hearts.
What was inside them became visible around them.
Complaint. Unbelief. Contempt.
Bitten by the very death they kept flirting with.
But here’s what we miss—

This story is not only about snakes.
It is about sin.
And sin still bites.

The tongue that keeps murmuring.
The heart that keeps accusing God.
The soul that keeps saying, “What You’ve given me is not enough.”
That road always ends in venom.
And yet grace walks into the scene.

Because later in this chapter, God tells Moses to lift up the bronze serpent.
Whoever looked in faith would live.
And Jesus takes that shocking image and says it pointed to Himself.

Lifted up.
So the poisoned could live.

This is the Gospel:
We were not dying because life was unfair.
We were dying because sin had already entered the bloodstream.
But Christ was lifted up on the cross so that everyone who looks to Him in faith will not perish, but have eternal life.

So do not just fear the snakes.
Fear the hard heart that complains against a holy God.
And do not stay there.

Repent.
Look to Jesus.
Live.

The same God who judged sin made a way for sinners to be healed.
That is not contradiction.
That is holy mercy.
